title: Breast Anatomy: Mammary Lobules, Ducts & Lymph Drainage
description: Explore breast anatomy over the anterior chest wall, including mammary lobes, terminal duct lobular units, lactiferous ducts, Cooper ligaments, and glands.
h1: Breast Anatomy: Mammary Lobules, Lactiferous Ducts and Lymphatics
blurb: Mammary glandular lobules and converging lactiferous ducts supported by fibrous Cooper ligaments over the pectoral fascia, with key axillary lymphatic drainage.
lead: Positioned over the pectoralis major muscle inside the superficial fascia of the chest wall, the breast combines specialized glandular lobules with fibrous suspensory support. In this illustrated guide to female breast anatomy, we examine 20 documented structures—including lobules (glandular), lactiferous ducts, subareolar lactiferous ducts, nipple—linking regional topography, tissue architecture, physiological mechanisms, and clinical reasoning.
overview: Positioned over the pectoralis major muscle inside the superficial fascia of the chest wall, the breast combines specialized glandular lobules with fibrous suspensory support. Female breast in cut-away with every ductal and structural part; the male breast is the same blueprint, undeveloped. Within the human body, the breast (Mamma / Glandula mammaria) is situated in pectoral region, T2–T6 ribs, receives arterial perfusion via internal thoracic + lateral thoracic arteries, and is innervated by intercostal nerves T2–T6 + lactiferous reflex.

Structurally, the lobules (glandular) (Lobuli glandulae) comprises secretory alveolar clusters at duct ends. Physiologically, the lobules (glandular) governs milk production under prolactin. The lactiferous ducts (Ductus lactiferi) are 15–20 branching channels to the nipple. Physiologically, the lactiferous ducts transport milk. The subareolar lactiferous ducts (Ductus lactiferi) are branching ducts converge near the nipple; classic large lactiferous sinuses are not consistently seen on ultrasound. Physiologically, the subareolar lactiferous ducts carry milk from alveoli and lobules toward nipple openings, rather than acting as a major storage reservoir. Structurally, the nipple (Papilla mammaria) comprises pigmented projection with 15–20 duct openings. Physiologically, the nipple governs milk delivery; erotic sensation. Structurally, the areola (Areola mammae) comprises pigmented ring with sebaceous Montgomery tubercles. Physiologically, the areola governs lubrication and latch cue. Structurally, the adipose tissue (Corpus adiposum) comprises fat between glandular compartments. Physiologically, the adipose tissue governs size and contour.

Clinically, regarding the lobules (glandular), most breast cancers start in lobules or ducts. From a diagnostic standpoint, in the lactiferous ducts, ductal carcinoma in situ stays inside this lining. In clinical pathology involving the subareolar lactiferous ducts, a blocked duct may cause a localized tender area; ultrasound revised the older “sinus reservoir” model. Medical evaluation of the nipple also notes that paget's disease: eczema-like nipple change = cancer until proven otherwise.

questions.question: What structures make up breast tissue?
questions.answer: Breast tissue includes glandular lobules, a branching duct network, connective-tissue support, fat, vessels and nerves. Ducts open at the nipple.

questions.question: Are breast lobules and milk ducts the same thing?
questions.answer: No. Lobules contain milk-producing units; ducts transport secretions toward the nipple. Both are embedded in supporting connective and fatty tissue.

questions.question: What are the glandular lobules of the breast?
questions.answer: Glandular lobules are clusters of milk-secreting alveoli within the breast.

questions.question: Where are the lactiferous ducts located?
questions.answer: Lactiferous ducts pass through the breast from glandular lobules toward openings at the nipple.

questions.question: What is the function of the axillary lymph nodes?
questions.answer: Axillary lymph nodes filter lymph from the upper limb and much of the breast.
